title: Independent plumbing contractors
hypothesis: A public plumbing-specific source can improve trade and activity evidence, but a named licensee, permit contractor, or published dispatch number is only an owner/contact candidate until separate ownership, line, reachability, and DNC gates pass.
ownerSource: Existing Maps-first discovery plus any lawfully usable state plumbing register or permit record that names a contractor; no current implemented plumbing register proves ownership.
phoneSource: Published business numbers from Maps; Austin permits also expose contractor_phone in the exact adapter query. Neither is owner-confirmed or phone-verified by this review.

workflow.label: Plumbing business input
workflow.detail: Start with the live recipe-A Maps discovery query for plumber and retain a named business candidate.

workflow.label: Plumbing relevance
workflow.detail: Require plumbing or a core plumbing term; adjacent HVAC, septic, excavation, or water-heater-only results do not establish plumbing fit.

workflow.label: Off-trade or ambiguous result
workflow.detail: Reject or hold an adjacent-only or generic contractor result for review.

workflow.label: License or permit candidate
workflow.detail: Where a source is available and lawful, use an active plumbing record only to corroborate trade, business, and a named candidate role.

workflow.label: No corroborating identity
workflow.detail: Keep the Maps business contact as a business lead; do not infer an owner from a missing register or permit match.

workflow.label: Named plumbing candidate
workflow.detail: Retain licensee or permit-contractor role as candidate evidence only; an employee, qualifier, or permit filer may not own the company.

workflow.label: Published business contact gate
workflow.detail: Evaluate only a published business contact through the existing line-type, live, DNC, duplicate, and ownership-evidence gates.

workflow.label: Deliver after all gates
workflow.detail: Deliver only after independent owner evidence and authorized contact/compliance outcomes pass.

failures.risk: A plumbing licensee, qualifier, or permit contractor is represented as the business owner.
failures.mitigation: Persist the source role as candidate evidence and require independent ownership evidence before owner labeling or delivery.

failures.risk: A dispatch, shared office, or franchise number is represented as a direct owner mobile.
failures.mitigation: Keep published numbers as business contacts until normal line-type, DNC, dedupe, and ownership gates pass.

failures.risk: Adjacent drain, septic, excavation, HVAC, or water-heater results contaminate a plumbing cohort.
failures.mitigation: Use the plumbing profile's core-term match; route adjacent-only and generic results to hold or reject.

failures.risk: An unfiltered sparse sample is mistaken for a removed source schema.
failures.mitigation: Repeat the exact adapter select and where before disabling a source. Root reproduced HTTP 200 with all required fields on five rows.

failures.risk: Texas TSBPE is treated as a free bulk plumbing source.
failures.mitigation: Keep TSBPE bulk fields, price, and terms UNKNOWN; use only a separately verified lawful source before implementation.

iterations.hypothesis: The Austin open permit route supplies a current plumbing contractor name and published contractor phone as activity/contact-candidate evidence.
iterations.test: Free live schema sample of 20 rows from data.austintexas.gov/resource/3syk-w9eu.json on 2026-09-24; retain aggregate field presence only.
iterations.observed: Worker reported missing contractor fields in an unfiltered 20-row sample and a 400 response; the failure did not reproduce with the configured query. This observation does not establish schema removal.
iterations.change: Do not disable the adapter from a sparse unfiltered sample. Reproduce its exact query first.

iterations.hypothesis: The exact configured Austin query remains usable.
iterations.test: Root requested permit_number, contractor_trade, contractor_company_name, contractor_full_name, contractor_phone, contractor_zip, issue_date with issue_date after 2025-09-24 and contractor_phone IS NOT NULL; limit 5.
iterations.observed: HTTP 200; 5 rows; all seven selected fields present across the response. No contact values retained.
iterations.change: Keep the existing adapter. Plumbing-specific trade filtering and route integration remain proposed; no current phone-yield claim.

measurement.result: Root reproduction: exact configured Austin query returned HTTP 200 and 5 rows with the seven selected fields represented. Earlier worker schema-failure inference was not reproduced. No phone, ownership, or compliance outcomes measured.

cost.basis: Free public endpoint schema sample only; no paid discovery, append, or verification was invoked.
cost.note: No clean owner-contact outcome was measured, so cost per clean contact is unknown.

implementation.summary: Plumbing remains recipe A with relevance classification. Austin adapter is implemented and its exact query works, but it is not mapped to this industry; a plumbing-specific trade filter is still required.

nextMeasurement: Audit 5-20 plumbing-filtered Austin records with separate distinct-business, role and business-contact-field counts, then independently authorized contact verification. No replacement endpoint is necessary on current evidence.
